research_notes: A robust final relay contract should specify what happens when the next task estimate is missing: default to conservative bounded-unit admission near cutoff.
It should also specify what happens when close-overhead history is sparse: use a wider fixed reserve rather than adaptive guessing.
When workload is unusually large/non-interruptible, handoff should occur before starting it if the hard-cap budget cannot safely contain it.
When workload units are very small, a soft-cutoff policy can continue productive work closer to hard cap.
These rules align the eventual policy with actual task granularity rather than a rigid one-size threshold.
The current boundary phase supplies the hard envelope needed before those decisions can be tuned.
